newsitem.title: USA: Bayou Steel Tennessee labor contract signed.
newsitem.headline: Bayou Steel Tennessee labor contract signed.

text.p: Bayou Steel Corp said Wednesday it entered into a seven-and-a-half year contract with United Steelworkers of America Local No. 9410 which the local's members ratified May 16.

The pact covers nearly 100 members in the collective bargaining unit at the Harriman facility, 40 miles west of Knoxville, Tenn. Talks began last Fall after Bayou recognized the union, the company explained.
The contract has no impact on Bayou's Louisiana mini-mill, where the company and union entered into an agreement on Sept 23, 1996, following a three-and-a-half year strike.

The new Tennessee contract builds on the type of operating flexibility the company established in its earlier contract settlement in Louisiana, according to Hank Vasquez, vice president of human resources.

He said the contract provides hourly wage increases totaling $0.80 over its life, plus opportunities for additional pay through a production incentive plan, a pay-for-knowledge plan, and a profit-sharing plan.

There is cost-shared medical and dental coverage to employees; several newly created and upgraded job classifications which will result in higher levels of pay for certain positions; unchanged levels of vacations, holidays, life insurance and 401K plan and an undisclosed signing bonus.
Bayou has maintained since 1993 that in order to be a low cost producer and compete successfully, it must have wages tied to production, the company noted.

In the March quarter, Bayou Steel noted, the company reported its first earnings since the 1996's June quarter -- partly based on improvements at the Tennessee facility. The company reported a 43 percent reduction in conversion costs and a 100 percent increase in production levels over the prior year, and expects to see continued improvement.
